messages:
maya: heads up — since the kernel bump on the us-west-2 GPU fleet I'm seeing intermittent pod->pod streaming pauses during large model shard transfers. Alerts spiked at 10:02 and several NCCL/gRPC streams hit timeouts.
ashwin: any packet logs or tcpdump? are we seeing ICMP "fragmentation needed"?
maya: grabbed a tcpdump from one affected pod pair. saw a bunch of `IP frag` / `ICMP frag needed` coming from node egress, then long retransmit gaps. snippet:```10:02:14.123456 IP hostA > hostB: IP frag 1/2 ...\n10:02:14.123457 ICMP hostB > hostA: Fragmentation needed and DF set (mtu = 1450)```
priya: nodes have mixed NIC configs after the rolling kernel upgrade — some still advertise 9000 on mlx5, overlay VXLAN interface on others is 1450. Could be GSO/TSO interaction with encapsulation.
liam: interesting — RDMA path should bypass VXLAN, but fallback paths hit overlay on some nodes. Did the upgrade change iptables/nft rules or CNI behaviour?
maya: CNI (calico) has mtu 1450 set in daemonset, but a subset of nodes ended up with vxlan0 mtu 1500 due to a race in init script. packets >1450 are getting through native NIC but then encapsulated, causing fragments on egress.
nashwin: quick checks to run on impacted node: `ip -d link show dev vxlan.calico`, `ip link show dev eth0`, `ethtool -k eth0 | grep -E "gso|tso|gro"`, `dmesg | tail -n50` — look for offload and TSO/GSO errors.
priya: also check `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing` and `ip route get <dest>` to see path MTU behaviour. I suspect offload + wrong vxlan MTU = large SKBs that get chopped by encap and confuse gRPC streaming windows.
liam: temp mitigation: clamp overlay MTU to 1400 across nodes and disable TSO on vxlan iface with `ethtool -K vxlan0 tso off gso off gro off` in a daemonset. That should stop fragmentation until we fix init ordering.
maya: agrees — will push a quick-runbook: 1) daemonset to enforce vxlan MTU=1400, 2) netem tests to reproduce (send 9000-byte UDP payloads through pods), 3) roll nodes in small batches.
nashwin: I'll prep a kube job to run `iperf3`/`pktgen` and a tcpdump capture collector.
priya: long term: make the CNI config authoritative and add a node-level admission/repair that fixes MTU on boot. Also audit RDMA bypass logic — don't want RDMA fallback via overlay.
liam: opening incident ticket and tagging infra oncall, adding template: impact=streaming stalls, probable cause=mtu mismatch + offload, mitigation=clamp vxlan MTU + disable TSO on overlay, owner=maya, ETA patch rollout 30m. @sre-bot please generate incident doc. :thumbsup:
sre-bot: incident created: INC-202303-87, channel #incidents, assigned to oncall.
maya: rolling the mtu-clamp daemonset now, will update in 10.
nashwin: if anyone sees persistent stalls after clamp, we'll need to roll kernel rollback for the smallest cohort and continue debugging NIC firmware and CNI init-order bug.
priya: noted — I'll follow up with CNI PR to add a preflight that ensures vxlan MTU matches CNI config and restarts kubelet if mismatch persists.
maya: update: after clamp, retransmit spikes dropped to near-zero on first two nodes. keeping the mitigation in place until we patch init. thanks all. :party_parrot:
